chunks: From him, from ʿUbays, from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, who said:

I heard al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام while he was saying: “Indeed, the beginning of the time of ẓuhr is the sun’s decline from the meridian, and the end of its time is one qāmah from the decline; and the beginning of the time of ʿaṣr is one qāmah, and the end of its time is two qāmahs.” I said, “Is it the same in winter and summer?” He said, “Yes.”
And we have already explained earlier that the qāmah and the dhirāʿ are expressions referring to one and the same thing, and what he narrated confirms that:

key_terms.أَوَّلَ وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the beginning of the time for ẓuhr salat (prayer)
key_terms.أَوَّلَ وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the beginning of the time for ʿaṣr salat (prayer)
key_terms.الذِّرَاعَ: the cubit measure, stated here as equivalent to qāmah
key_terms.الشِّتَاءِ: winter, mentioned to clarify seasonal consistency of the ruling
key_terms.الصَّيْفِ: summer, mentioned to clarify seasonal consistency of the ruling
key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the entry of ẓuhr time
key_terms.قَامَةٌ: a unit of measured shadow length used here to define prayer time intervals
key_terms.قَامَتَانِ: two qāmahs, indicating the end point mentioned for ʿaṣr time

ai.seo_question: What are the times of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr salat according to the hadith of al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the beginning and end of the preferred times for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr salat (prayer), beginning from the sun’s decline and measured by qāmah intervals. It also clarifies that this ruling applies equally in winter and summer, and notes that qāmah and dhirāʿ refer to the same measure in this context.
